I tested 6 AI writing tools for a month. Here's what stuck.

I write release notes and support docs for a 12-person SaaS team. In August I paid for six tools out of pocket and used each one on real tickets for about five days. Total cost was $148, which I am now slightly annoyed about.

Two of them earned a place in my week. WriteFlow is decent at turning a messy Slack thread into a first-draft changelog entry, but it invents version numbers if you don't paste them in. I caught it twice. CopyNest was the worst for docs: every answer came back padded with a paragraph about why documentation matters, which nobody asked for.

The tool I kept is the boring one. It rewrites a sentence when I highlight it and otherwise stays out of the way. I turned off its "tone" feature on day two because it kept making our error messages sound cheerful.

What I learned: the time saving is real for summaries of long threads, maybe 20 minutes a day. For anything a customer reads, I still write it myself and use the tool to catch typos. If you only try one, try the cheapest one with a highlight-to-rewrite feature and see if you open it again after a week.

My notes spreadsheet, with every prompt I used and what came back, is linked at the bottom. Some of the outputs are funny. One tool described our password reset page as "a journey of rediscovery."
